mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that increase recession risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 4.5% in the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS have increased by at least 0.5% in the prior month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained economy (as indicated by INDPRO growth below 1.0% annually), manufacturing output stagnation reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO growth is below 1.0% annually, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has increased for the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger premature monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market boom (as indicated by HOUST above 1500 thousand units), strong residential construction activity drives consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST exceeds 1500 thousand units, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls in the same month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.
